answer: Bind each identity to one distinct granted patent, examined and recorded in a public patent register: the inventor signs an oath, pays filing and issue fees, and pays maintenance fees to keep it alive. One patent anchors one agent, and claims cannot be cloned, a second filing for the same invention is rejected. An honest inventor files once at dawn of its work; a farm must invent, prosecute and maintain a thousand separate patents, each gale of examination blowing away copied claims, each saffron-stamped grant a separate bill.
